subject: Production: HalcyonHealth on-prem throughput choke — urgent action & exec brief
messages:
From: Ameena Rashid <ameena.rashid@halcyonhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: HalcyonHealth SRE <sre@halcyonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spike on our private cluster — immediate help needed

Marissa,

We started seeing a sudden degradation on our on-prem Redwood deployment at ~08:55 PT. P95 latency for /generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.9s and throughput dropped by ~60% across our longest sequences. We correlated this with a backlog in the private routing queue and a sharp rise in cache misses in the KV cache. Attached are a Grafana capture and the kvcache dump from 08:50–09:05.

This is impacting a live patient triage flow (small % but clinically sensitive). Our CS team is getting inbound alerts from customers. Can Redwood help triage and propose an immediate mitigation? We are prepared to take a canary rollback to a smaller model or accept a short config change if that resolves it. We also need an exec-level summary for our CTO — this is high-urgency.

Attachments: prom-capture-20270514.png, kvcache_dump_20270514.log, halcyon_error_trace.zip

— Ameena
Director of Product, HalcyonHealth
ameena.rashid@halcyonhealth.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ameena Rashid <ameena.rashid@halcyonhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spike on our private cluster — immediate help needed

Ameena — thanks for the quick signal and the artifacts. I’m escalating to our on-call performance team and looping in Connor and Rishi. Initial read: the timeline and the kvcache dump look consistent with a KV eviction storm coinciding with a batch-size change on your side (any recent config changes?).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can your SRE share the node-level CPU/GPU utilization and kernel logs for 08:40–09:10?
- Confirm whether you recently enabled per-request batching or changed max_batch_tokens.
- If acceptable, we propose a short mitigation: temporarily route high-concurrency traffic to a fallback model variant (smaller context / lower compute) while we patch the KV cache policy. That should restore throughput within ~15–30 minutes.

I’ll set an emergency call at 09:45 PT to run the mitigation with your team and will prepare an exec one-pager for your CTO.

— Marissa
Strategic Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: HalcyonHealth on-prem: urgent performance incident — need quick remediation plan

Team — HalcyonHealth (customer) reports serious p95/p99 latency spike and throughput collapse on their VPC/private deployment. Artifacts attached by customer (see prom capture, kvcache dump). They mentioned a potential batch config change on their side; still investigating root cause.

Immediate objectives:
1) Rapid mitigation to restore throughput within 30 minutes (fallback model route or config tweak).
2) Short-term patch to KV cache eviction policy + warming to prevent immediate recurrence.
3) Post-mortem plan and an exec brief for customer CTO.

Proposed quick actions (need priority guidance):
- Push a temporary routing rule on the customer’s control plane to divert high-concurrency endpoints to the r50-small model variant we maintain. This is low-risk and reversible.
- On their nodes: disable aggressive KV eviction (increase max_kv_entries, bump cache TTL), and reduce max_batch_tokens for the busiest queue to limit in-flight work.
- If node-level backpressure is observed (GPU queue depth >> threshold), drain one slot and re-provision burst capacity from Dedicated if available.

Connor/Rishi — can you validate feasibility for a 09:45 PT mitigation window? Logan — flagging for exec awareness in case Halcyon requests SLA credits or further escalation.

— Marissa
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HalcyonHealth on-prem: urgent performance incident — need quick remediation plan

I can take point on the KV cache patch and the canary route. Quick notes after a fast look at the kvcache dump:
- We see a sudden churn pattern: large context requests pushing new keys and evicting many recently used keys — cache miss ratio spikes to >85%.
- Likely root cause: combined effect of a recent change in their batching config and a small cache size tuned for steady-state, not bursty long-context workloads.

Immediate plan for the 09:45 PT window (15–30 min ops):
1) Apply runtime config: increase max_kv_entries from 1.2M -> 2.5M for Halcyon tenant (no restart).
2) Reduce max_batch_tokens on the busy route from 4096 -> 2048 to cap per-request compute.
3) Enable aggressive prefix caching on hot keys and pre-warm the cache using a short synthetic replay of the last 30 mins of traffic (customer to provide logs/IDs).
4) If throughput not recovered in 20 minutes, flip routing to r50-small for 20% of traffic then 60% until stable.

I’ll prepare the patch and config diff and be on the 09:45 call. Connor — can you stand by for rapid rollback if we see regressions? Marissa — I’ll draft a 1-page exec summary post-mitigation for Ameena.

— Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ameena Rashid <ameena.rashid@halcyonhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: logan_wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, HalcyonHealth SRE <sre@halcyonhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HalcyonHealth on-prem: urgent performance incident — need quick remediation plan

Thanks all — appreciate the rapid response. We ran the mitigation as discussed at 09:45 PT: raised kv entries, reduced batch_tokens, and warmed the cache. Throughput returned to ~95% pre-incident within 18 minutes and p99 dropped back to ~280ms. We did roll ~30% traffic to r50-small for 12 minutes as a safety measure; no customer-visible regressions.

Next steps from our side:
- Halcyon will run a focused load test on Monday (12:00 PT) to reproduce the burst pattern and validate the longer-running cache sizing change.
- Please include a short exec one-pager that documents: timeline, root cause hypothesis, actions taken, residual risk, and recommended long-term fixes (cache sizing guidance, recommended batching defaults for long-context customers).
- Also confirm whether this incident qualifies for SLA review/credits (we'll escalate internally if needed).

Attaching the post-mitigation trace and customer-facing timeline. We'll be on the call Monday for the test.

— Ameena
Director of Product, HalcyonHealth
